data.title: Web Hosting
data.tagline: A service that continuously stores and serves website files or a running environment
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish hosting, which continuously serves a site, from deployment, which publishes a version, and verify hosting through a public URL.
data.description: A page that works locally still needs a public environment that can serve it continuously. Web hosting provides that environment for files or a running service; deployment is the one-time action of publishing a version into it. They are related but not the same.

learning.assumes: You can open a website locally or have seen a project published to a public address.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish hosting, which continuously serves a site, from deployment, which publishes a version, and verify hosting through a public URL.

explanation.title: Hosting is the persistent environment
explanation.text: It stores static files or keeps a request-serving service running. When people use a public address, the environment returns the page or service result.

explanation.title: Deployment is the action that puts a version there
explanation.text: A deployment publishes one build or code version into the hosting environment. A successful build or a domain alone does not prove the public site serves the right version.

data.boundary: Hosting is the long-lived environment that serves a site; deployment is a version-release action; a domain and DNS direct an address to a target. Hosting does not automatically provide a custom domain, database, or correct version, so verify with a public request.

lessonPractice.title: The platform has assigned a runtime environment, but the public page still shows the old version. What should you check first?

options.label: Check whether the latest deployment published the right version, then inspect the public URL
options.feedback: Correct. The hosting environment exists, so an old version points to the deployment input or result. Check which version was published where.

options.label: Create another hosting environment and have both serve the page
options.feedback: An existing environment does not explain the old version. First check the target environment and the version used by the deployment.

options.label: Change DNS only because the domain determines which version is served
options.feedback: A domain and DNS direct requests to a destination, but they do not publish a new version into that environment. Check deployment instead.

data.agentPrompt: First confirm whether this project needs static file hosting or a continuously running service, then deploy it to the matching hosting environment. Request the page through its public URL and verify the new version rather than localhost; if it is still old, separate a hosting-environment issue from a deployment-version issue.
